title: Color
text: Well, if I act too recklessly, my Father’s life will likely be in danger. If I were to take on dangerous quests at the Adventurers’ Guild to make money, having powerful allies would surely result in assassins being sent after my Father. However, to earn my Father’s trust, I’ll have to save him right then and there.

In the first world, my Father became embittered because he had no one on his side. I absolutely cannot let Father go through such a painful experience again. That being the case, the key is how quickly I can make him strong enough to survive an attack by assassins.

……As I mulled it over, a few ideas came to mind. There’s nothing better than actually trying them out. I slowly cast the Portal Spear while playfully teasing Filolial-sama, and checked the list of places I could travel to.

Skills have been unlocked that allow me to increase the number of destinations accessible via these portals for weapon enhancement and make managing registered locations easier. As a result, a list of accessible locations within my field of view has appeared to some extent. And even if I loop through these locations… they don’t disappear. My previous runs are by no means wasted.

Siltvelt… This is a country that worships my Father and harbors dangerous ideologies; in that sense, it’s quite similar to Melromarc. But since Father is generally receptive to what my father-in-law has to say, there’s no reason not to take advantage of that.

However, it’s also true that we must avoid bringing Father along in public. To prevent a war, we’ll have to stay in Melromarc, but there’s no need to impose unnecessary restrictions on ourselves. When the time comes—yes… let’s make use of him.

Well, it’ll be soon enough. Thinking it through, I believe secretly collaborating with Siltvelt is a brilliant idea. Mm-hmm. It makes it easier to imagine the future. While deducing the path my Father first took, I’ll streamline things to make him and his group stronger.
Next is acquiring Filo-tan. How can I become Filo-tan’s master? I have absolutely no idea where my Father bought her—it’s like trying to grasp at clouds.

If I followed historical fact… I might be able to figure out where to get her, but my pride won’t allow it. There’s no way I could ever treat my Father harshly. Besides, if I had to live with the Crimson Swine for even a month, I might just go crazy.

…I suppose I have no choice. I’ll just have to search for her, like looking for a jewel lost in the desert. To begin with… even if Filo-tan were to belong to someone else, I, Motoyasu, am absolutely certain I could find her.

First of all, Filo-tan’s color scheme is actually quite rare. Filolial-sama are almost always a single color. This is especially evident with Queens and Kings. Not to mention Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan—even Ku, Marine, and Midori have a base color that covers most of their bodies.

While there are areas where other colors appear, those parts are white. In other words… Sakura-chan’s color scheme is the closest match. Hers is based on a cherry blossom pink—the exact opposite of Filo-tan’s—with white mixed in. However, Filo-tan’s base color is white, with a touch of cherry blossom pink. Even Filolial-sama has this color scheme, you know.

Another major difference is eye color. While their eyes are often the same color as their body, Filo-tan’s eyes are blue. In other words, even if Filo-tan were unable to become the Filolial Queen and ended up belonging to someone else, it wouldn’t be impossible to find her if you keep these two points in mind.
I, Motoyasu, have no intention of giving up on finding Filo-tan. No matter how many years it takes, and even if I end up saving the world, I will definitely find Filo-tan. All right! My plan is set.
“Gua!”
After finishing my duties with Filolial-sama, I gave a quick nod to the soldier serving as her attendant, then hurried toward the shadow of a building inside the castle.
“‘Boo-boo!’”
They’re following me, aren’t they? But your pursuit ends here. The moment I step into the shadow of the building, I’ll use my Portal Spear to teleport.
In an instant, my view shifted, and I found myself in front of that vast Filolial Ranch!
“Excuse me!”
I immediately called out to the farmer at the Filolial Ranch. This time, he was in the management hut.
“Who’s there?”
“A visitor.”
“Answering ‘visitor’ when asked who you are… Well, fine. So? What brings you here?”
“I’d like to ask for one of the eggs that Filolial-sama is hatching.”
“You… do you even know what kind of ranch this is?”
This back-and-forth is exactly the same as last time. The farmer, sitting in the manager’s hut looking annoyed, propped his elbow on the table and replied.
“But…”
The farmer is staring at me intently. Oh, come to think of it, I’m still wearing the same clothes I had when I was first summoned.
“You’re dressed pretty strangely, aren’t you?”
“My outfit isn’t a problem.”
“It’s not up to you to decide that!”
Huh? It seems I’ve been called out on something. But I know one thing for sure: this farmer, who raises Filolials, truly loves Filolial-sama.
“Anyway, I’d like you to sell me Filolial-sama’s eggs.”
“That’s what I’ve been telling you—I can’t part with the Filolials from here. If you really want them, I’ll sell you eggs laid elsewhere.”
“I’m not picky. If you’re going to sell them, I’d like you to do it quickly.”
“Why do you want a Filolial so badly?”
It seems this is some sort of test, in this farmer’s own way. But my answer remains the same.
There’s no particular reason. I raise them simply because Filolial-sama exists. There’s no room for rational thought in this matter. That is the rule of the world.

If I had to say, Filolial-sama is a noble being, akin to gods, created from love. That is why I raise them and cherish them. All the Filolial-samas are equally my sons and daughters. The only exceptions are Filo-tan and the large Filolial-sama.
“A world without the Filolial-samas has no right to exist. Yes… the Filolial-samas are the world’s greatest treasure, and to me, they are like the air I breathe.”
“What nonsense… You desire them so much, yet you have no particular preferences?”
“I love Filolial-sama equally. Yes… just like my own children—whether they’re quick or slow, strong or weak, smart or silly—I love them all equally… That is the reason for my existence…”
“…Do you really love Filolial-sama?”
“Of course I do.”
The farmer looked at me with a serious expression.
“Well then… let’s try a quiz. If you can answer it, I’ll sell it to you.”

With that, the farmer stood up, stepped out of the management shed, and gave me a quiz on identifying Filolial-sama’s varieties. For someone like Motoyasu, these were all questions easier than twisting a baby’s hand.
“That’s amazing… I’ve never seen anyone with such deep knowledge of Filolial-sama before.”

“I always think this about the Filolial-sama here—there’s a part of their health management that seems like it could break down at any moment and is a bit dangerous. It’s best not to worry too much about a little weight gain.”
“I’m not here to hear your idealistic theories. Then you prove it to me using the eggs I gave you.”
“Understood!”
Last time, I was too busy to show you how Yuki-chan and the others had grown. I, Motoyasu, intend to keep my promises as much as possible.
“So? What’s the budget, and how many do you want?”
I’ve received a stipend this time, so I have more money than last time. However, I can’t afford to spend that much just to invest in Father. I’ll hold up three fingers.
“Three… Alright, one can be a good one, but the other two can be cheap ones, right?”
“No problem at all.”

That’s right… I won’t discriminate against any of the Filolial-sama. But as a parent, I’d naturally want to reunite with them if possible… I was led to a nearby warehouse where Filolial eggs are stored. Just like last time, the farmer brought one “special” egg from the back and two “bonus” ones from the front.
“That won’t do.”
“Huh?”
That’s right—if my memory serves me correctly, the eggs the farmer chose were different from the ones last time.
“From the back, take the one on the right; from the front, these two here are the ones I want.”
I pointed out the eggs that I believed belonged to Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan.
“Are you sure about that? This combination is better, you know?”
Holding one of the eggs from the back, the farmer replied.
“It’s fine.”
“Hmm… Well, these are worth less, so that’s fine, but you really are a strange one.”
I touched the eggs the farmer handed me and, relying on my memory, double-checked their texture. …There’s no doubt about it—these are Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan’s eggs!
“Thank you so much!”
“Come show them to me if you have time.”
“Got it! I’ll come show you these kids once they’ve grown into the legendary Filolial-sama!”
This time, I’ll definitely go show them to him. No, once things settle down a bit, I’ll go buy some more.
“Hmph. ‘Legendary Filolial,’ huh? You’re really laying it on thick… I’ll be looking forward to it.”
“Well then, goodbye.”
And so, having once again obtained Yuki-chan and the others’ eggs, I returned to Melromarc.
